I'm an American and I do live permanently in Germany. I wasn't actually unaccompanied as my wife is German, but here if you have an IT degree you can get a pretty good job. Germany is currently needing more workers in technical related fields. Germany has a pretty decent health system (even if it is a universal health system). The beer is also really good. There's always a difference between visiting and staying permanently. Once you live away from other Americans you tend to start getting the feel for the way Germans do things. I've been an expat for 16 years in 3 different countries. I can empathize. And yes... I fully agree, why are Germans so insane? Working for a German company is sometimes a form of self punishment I think. :)

Depends on how you deal with cultural alienation. If you don't think you'd be able to cope with being surrounded by people who don't speak your language or communicate with you, then countries like Australia or anywhere in the UK might be a good choice. Canada is likely the closest thing to US without actually being the US, so if you're trying to distance yourself from specific US legislation (for example) without abandoning the culture entirely this might be a good choice.

If cultural alienation isn't a concern for you at all and you're interested in a neat adventure there a few different places you could try, a couple of which I've lived in myself:

-Bangkok - can be a little bit hectic, but it's dirt cheap to live here and very interesting culturally. Once you're out of the city the scenery is gorgeous. The cultural alienation was a bit much for me (I'll be returning to Canada fairly soon) but if that's not a concern this place is a blast.

-Hong Kong - can also be kind of crazy, but it's actually quite developed at this point. Unlike Bangkok it was colonized a little while ago so the cultural differences are not quite so apparent, though it is still extremely interesting and beautiful.

-Panama - Not as developed as somewhere like Hong Kong, but the culture is shifting towards a more american view. Panama City is a city of contrasts to say the least and you very quickly transition from glamorous, upscale buildings to the depths of poverty where quite a few local people are trapped. Tons of exotic wildlife and landscapes - you feel like you're on a grand adventure the entire time you're there (Haven't lived here, but visited for just over a month)

-Spain - My experience in Spain was fantastic, though I was only there for a couple of months. Though reasonably developed the streets still have a certain cozy feel to them which is very comfortable. Language might be an issue here, though more and more people are starting to speak basic english (and quite a few speak it very well) from what I've heard.

Interesting point. I think it may be worth discussing which experience should have less friction: creating a subverse? Or admin takeover?

I don't have the right answer, but to me creation should be pretty easy. I'll admit I haven't thought through the ramificaitons of reducing friction of taking over a subverse. This could incentive hostile takeovers in the future. Thoughts?

If the criteria for takeover are very well laid out then it there doesn't need to be much friction in some circumstances Examples:

  • Sub with no posts and inactive for two days
  • Sub with no subscribers and minimal posts

The more complicated situations would require admins contacting the owner, so that if it is necessary to takeover then it is done fairly and with input from the owner.

So all in all it would come down to the admins creating a very clear public policy on how it should be done and when it can be done.

The Voat rules on this are that each moderator needs to fulfill the following:

In a 30-day period, contribute to at least one discussion. In a 30-day period, either share a link or start at least one discussion.

Full text and source from the Voat FAQ:

While Voat is in alpha, we will be freeing up unused/inactive subs by deleting them or transferring them to users who submit a subverse transfer request in /v/subverserequest. As a subverse owner, at least once a month, you should start at least one discussion in your sub, or submit at least one link to your sub. Furthermore, at least once a month, you should submit at least one comment to a discussion/link posted in your sub. If you fail to do anything of the above, your sub will be considered as abandoned/inactive and it may be deleted or transferred to another user which makes a request in /v/subverserequest.

A well created or implemented policy should be sure to take into account the desired end result(s). I think minimizing hostile takeover is an important end result. Also important, and more so now I'd say, is the goal of bringing quality content to the site.

The easier subverse creation is, the more likely it is for people to create subverses for appropriate specialties and niches, and the more likely it is for people to find the specialized subverse and contribute.

When there is enough content that front page/communities are always fresh and active (totally open on how to make this determination), then implementing further steps to ensure new subverses are created only by competent and committed individuals would make more sense.
